title: Answer: degrees of consciousness reach beyond brains to tissues, organs and synthetic constructs

statements.text: No principled line restricts consciousness to sophisticated human-like brains, so degrees of consciousness must be considered in other organs, tissues and synthetic constructs that share the features of neurons and their networks. Systems that act in morphogenetic, transcriptional and other spaces should have some, if very minimal, degree of consciousness. A typical human is a patchwork of many consciousnesses, only one of which usually reports its states in words. Since some goal-directedness seems present even in particles, there may be no true zero, but mere accretion does not raise it: a rock is not more conscious than its particles, while biological organization amplifies it.
